latin: Nulla est uirtus in caelo_aut in terra seminaliter et separata quam et actuare et unire magus non possit.
translation: There is no power in the sky or on the earth, existing seminally and separately, that the magus cannot both actuate and unite.
translation_note: 'caelo' renders the celestial or astronomical realm, not heaven in the religious sense, throughout Pico's magical theses, per Farmer's note (farmer1998:25215); 'seminaliter et separata' are technical terms for powers latent in seed-form and for powers existing as discrete, scattered instances.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch17, from Latin at farmer1998:25190
doctrine: The thesis claims the magus's power to actuate and unite extends to every power latent or scattered in heaven and earth (farmer1998:25190). Farmer's note glosses 'caelum' here as the celestial realm rather than the religious heaven, and its text explicitly cross-references thesis 9>11 as making the same claim, using the abbreviated id notation of the underlying OCR (farmer1998:25215).
historiography: Akopyan (2018) and Akopyan (2021) both quote this thesis's Latin verbatim in a single footnote alongside 9>11's Latin, citing the two together, from consecutive pages of Pico's magic conclusions ('ibid., 5' and 'ibid., 11'), as paired statements of the magus's power over seminal and separated natural virtues (akopyan2018:580; akopyan2021:1338).
not_established: Whether Farmer's own discussion of this thesis extends beyond the shared gloss with 9>1 and the cross-reference to 9>11 is not established by the sources consulted.
